thread:
devon: heads-up — enabling warp_specialize on H100 for model-gpt2-like caused ~12% tail latency regression at seq=1024. autotuner picked tile=64x4 which increased reg pressure. anyone seen this?

maria: can you paste the nvprof / nsight snippet?

devon: ```
Kernel: attn_fwd_warp_specialized
Registers per thread: 96
Static SMem: 6400 bytes
Occupancy: 37%
gMangoProfile: cycles 1.12e9
```

anya: 96 regs is high. tile=64x4 means each thread holds bigger partial sums. can we try tile=32x8? that often trades regs for more smem but increases occupancy.

samir: also check KV cache path — when seq grows, we switch to 'long-seq' kernel; maybe autotuner incorrectly matched short-seq kernels. did autotuner consider seq bucket? :thinking:

devon: autotuner config snippet:
```json
{"seq_buckets": [128,256,512,1024], "candidates": ["tile_64x4","tile_32x8","tile_16x16"], "score": "latency+0.1*flops"}
```
It picked tile_64x4 for 1024 bc it beat latency on synthetic microbenchmarks but real workload includes KV cache misses + batching which changes memory access patterns.

maria: if autotuner doesn't simulate KV cache prefixing, synthetic bench could undercount memory-bound effects. suggest adding a 'kv_prefill' flag in the benchmark to reproduce.

anya: experiment plan: 1) run real workload with `tile_32x8, tile_16x16` on H100; 2) measure regs/spill/occupancy + p50/p99; 3) add `--kv-prefill 0.9` to simulate large prefix cache. i can run 1) this afternoon.

devon: ran quick A/B: tile_32x8 reduced regs to 72, occupancy -> 50%, p99 down 9% vs 64x4. but p50 slightly worse (1.6%); so autotuner's latency-only reward favored p50 for short microbenchmarks.

samir: we should change autotuner objective to penalize tail more for production. maybe `score: 0.7*p99 + 0.3*p50 + 0.1*memory`.

maria: also consider warp specialization guard: when tile_x >= 64, set `__launch_bounds__` or split into two kernels: one specialized for large tiles with register-limited variant and one for high-occupancy variant.

anya: or do dynamic kernel selection at runtime based on detected seq and kv-hit-rate. we already sample KV hit ratio in router. route >80% hits to high-throughput kernel, else to low-reg kernel.

devon: good point. current router exposes `kv_hit_estimate` in request metadata. i'll add a quick flag to runtime to pick kernel variant.

samir: watch out for code size & compile time explosion if we emit too many variants. limit to 3 per op.

maria: small nit — H100 has different per-SM register file than A100; autotuner should be architecture-aware: store "reg_limit" per arch and discard candidates that exceed capacity. we already have kernel descriptors but not enforced.

devon: yes, i saw candidate list didn't include arch caps. i'll add arch constraints and re-run global autotune overnight.

anya: for debug, please capture `nvprof --metrics sm_efficiency,reg_spill,shared_load_transactions` and attach.

devon: attached short dump in thread (paste below) — ran on H100.

```text
sm_efficiency: 0.76
reg_spill_stores: 12345
reg_spill_loads: 6789
shared_load_transactions: 4321
```

samir: looks like spill stores are non-trivial. reducing per-thread registers or splitting accumulators into shared memory could help.

maria: another lever: reduce unrolling for attention inner loop — unroll factor 4->2 lowers regs ~8-12 but adds loop overhead. worth trying.

devon: summary action items: 
- add arch-aware reg/smem caps to autotuner
- modify objective to weight p99
- add kv-prefill to bench harness
- implement runtime kernel variant switch using kv_hit_estimate
- run overnight global pass

anya: i'll run tile_32x8 and tile_16x16 perf jobs and post numbers tomorrow. :thumbsup:
